title: One-year myopia control efficacy of spectacle lenses with aspherical lenslets

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial; © Author(s) 2022, published by BMJ)

groups.description: spectacle lenses with highly aspherical lenslets (HAL; 11 concentric rings of contiguous aspherical lenslets), randomised 1:1:1, double-masked; Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China; 58 randomised, 54 completed 1 year (Table 1; mean age of completers)
spectacle lenses with slightly aspherical lenslets (SAL), randomised 1:1:1, double-masked; Wenzhou, China; 57 randomised, 55 completed 1 year (Table 1; mean age of completers)
single-vision spectacle lenses (SVL), randomised 1:1:1, double-masked; Wenzhou, China; 55 randomised, 52 completed 1 year (Table 1; mean age of completers)

cells.definition: definition:Methods (Statistical analysis): the change is the difference between baseline and the corresponding follow-up measurement; Table 2 unadjusted mean AL changes at 6 and 12 months; change at baseline is 0

series.baseline_label: Baseline AL (mm) of the 1-year completers, Table 1 (mean ± SE)
series.notes: unadjusted mean ± SE (Table 2 title and footnote; the linear-mixed-model adjusted means in the text and Fig 3 are not used); right eye of each child (Statistical analysis); Lenstar LS900; complete-case analysis of children who completed the 1-year visit; 54 of 58 randomised (93%) are tabulated (protocol inclusion 5: >=70%, admitted); 2 HAL children missed the 1-year visit and the rest of the shortfall were children not dispensed with study lenses

exclusions.what: Linear-mixed-model adjusted mean AL and SER changes (Results text, Fig 3)
exclusions.reason: model-adjusted estimates are not admissible (protocol inclusion 4); the unadjusted Table 2 means are used

exclusions.what: Table 2 P values; between-group differences and efficacy percentages (text)
exclusions.reason: p-values and comparisons are not admissible (protocol inclusion 4)

exclusions.what: Table 1 and Table 2 cycloplegic SER rows; Table 1 near phoria, accommodative lag, age of myopia onset, parental myopia; BCVA and wearing time (text)
Percentages of children with a decrease or no increase in AL or a myopic or hyperopic shift (text, online supplemental eFigure 1)

notes: Randomised double-masked trial ChiCTR1800017683 (2-year trial, 12-month interim analysis), Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China, started July 2018; 170 children randomised (HAL 58, SAL 57, SVL 55), 167 dispensed, 161 completed the 1-year visit (54, 55, 52); reasons for drop-out were stated as not related to the study device.
Baseline characteristics (Table 1) and changes (Table 2) are for the 1-year completers; data are means ± SE.
Refraction, phoria, accommodation and visual acuity are tabulated or reported but are not axial length.
